cases.evidence: first emitted piece asserted both frequencies were 2.4Ghz (contradicted)
cases.cause: head (second conjunct) had not arrived before committing
cases.proposed_rule: Do not finalize or cut after correlative structures ('both X and Y', 'either X or Y') until the second conjunct/head has appeared.

example_pair.input: The 802.11n standard operates on both the 2.4Ghz and 5.0Ghz frequencies.
example_pair.output: The 802.11n standard operates on <SEG:2> both the 2.4Ghz and 5.0Ghz frequencies <SEG:1>

cases.evidence: auxiliary chain split; translation rendered 'has been doing' as stative 'was' for the fragment
cases.cause: auxiliary (head) and main verb separated by a boundary before the lexical verb arrived
cases.proposed_rule: Never place a boundary inside an auxiliary+lexical-verb chain; wait for the main lexical verb after auxiliaries before finalizing the earlier fragment.

example_pair.input: At the other end of the spectrum, one morphs into an unrecognizable individual that feels he or she must change everything the team has been doing and make it their own.
example_pair.output: At the other end of the spectrum, one morphs into an unrecognizable individual that feels he or she must change everything the team has been doing <SEG:1> and make it their own <SEG:2>

cases.evidence: early fragment rendered 'lost' as 'was defeated' (object not yet seen) causing contradiction
cases.cause: verb ambiguous until its object/complement arrived; boundary broke verb--object link
cases.proposed_rule: Avoid finalizing an ambiguous verb's translation (e.g., 'lost') before its direct object/complement that disambiguates its sense has been observed.

example_pair.input: Giancarlo Fisichella lost control of his car and ended the race very soon after the start.
example_pair.output: Giancarlo Fisichella lost control of his car <SEG:1> and ended the race very soon after the start <SEG:2>

cases.evidence: fragment committed to action sense ('visit') and chose wrong sense for 'Shrine' before appositive clarified meaning
cases.cause: appositive/complement that disambiguates verb sense and label had not arrived
cases.proposed_rule: Delay committing to verb sense (existential vs. action) and to ambiguous place/label lexical choices until following noun-phrase complements or appositions have been seen.

example_pair.input: Also to the north visit the great Sanctuary of Our Lady of Fatima (Shrine), a place of worldwide famous Marian apparitions.
example_pair.output: Also to the north <SEG:2> visit the great Sanctuary of Our Lady of Fatima (Shrine), a place of worldwide famous Marian apparitions <SEG:1>

cases.evidence: negated report separated from its location phrase, producing awkward/partly contradictory output ordering
cases.cause: prepositional/localizing complement ('in the nation') was cut off from the predicate that it scopes over
cases.proposed_rule: Keep predicates together with their prepositional/location complements; do not cut between a negated report/predicate and its scope-establishing prepositional phrase.

example_pair.input: The Northern Marianas emergency management office said that there were no damages reported in the nation.
example_pair.output: The Northern Marianas emergency management office said that there were no damages reported in the nation <SEG:1>

summary: The prompt consistently places boundaries that separate heads (main verbs, lexical verbs, negated predicates) from the context that disambiguates them (objects, lexical verbs, appositives, locatives). Fixes should forbid boundaries inside auxiliary+verb chains, between verbs and their objects/complements, across correlative conjuncts, and between predicates and their scope-establishing prepositional phrases. Prioritization rules were not the primary issue in these cases.
